pageCache.pageTitle: Mora Primary School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
'Making a difference'
Mora is a vibrant, inclusive and welcoming school, which is well established within the local community. Children, parents and governors alike perceive Mora as a friendly and supportive extension of their family.
Vision
At Mora Primary and Nursery School we make a difference to our school community every day. We are proud to offer a strong foundation, upon which our pupils will build a successful future. We encourage our children to develop the ability to expect more of themselves whilst accepting that resilience is needed to secure success. Alongside this, our pupils develop an understanding of caring for themselves and for others, which leads to the greatest outcomes for all.
Values
We make the most of our time at Mora by laying the foundations for success:
Aiming High - We understand our capabilities and rise to our personal challenges.
Being Resilient - We push beyond our limits and value the sense of achievement this brings.
Caring for All - We have the strength of character to look out for ourselves and others.
Alongside our vision, Mora Primary And Nursery School promotes British values:
democracy
the rule of law
individual liberty
Home & School Agreement
It is important that the school, parents and children work together for the best outcomes for all.
Home & School Agreement

About Us
Use the menu to the right to learn more about Mora Primary and Nursery School.

Welcome
I am pleased to welcome you to our school website and I hope that it will give you a flavour of what Mora Primary School is all about.
Mora is a place of learning for all. We put success within the reach of all children and help them to achieve their full potential. Our school works hard to develop confident, reflective, creative learners that will grow into valued members of the community and make a positive contribution to twenty first century society.
Learning at Mora is fun and extends beyond the classroom. Special events and activities help to make our school an exciting place to be. Regular visits to places of interest enrich the children’s learning. Children are able to express themselves through the arts and music and there is a variety of music tuition available. Both indoor and outdoor physical activities play a vital contribution to our children’s well being.
Our children are guided and supported to grow and succeed academically, emotionally and spiritually.
Parents are partners in this process and are always welcome in our school. We will help you to understand and make the most of your child’s time in the school.
This website will provide some insight into what we believe makes our school distinctive, but I urge you to come and meet us, to feel the atmosphere and to judge for yourself what makes Mora Primary School a special place to work and learn.
Polly Baylis

Personal, Social and Health Education (PSHE) and RSE
PSHE at Mora

These are grouped into three core themes: health and wellbeing, relationships and living in the wider world (including economic wellbeing and aspects of careers education).

English (Reading, Writing and Spelling)
English at Mora
At Mora, English is an integral part of our curriculum. We aim for our children to become life-long learners, who love delving into books and the world. We want our children to develop a passion for writing and to be proud to share their work with others.
Reading:
The children participate in daily reading sessions. We ensure that good quality texts are at the core of our curriculum and drive learning in all subjects. We deliver a high-quality, skill and discussion based reading curriculum which enables children to develop fluency, read widely with confidence across both fiction and non-fiction texts and have meaningful discussions about what they have read. All children are taught a range of skills in reading to ensure that they not only become fluent readers but also have a good understanding of what they have read.
To encourage reading for pleasure, all children will have the opportunity to choose a home reading book from our library or their book corner, which is changed weekly. In addition, each child has a book allocated online, through Collins Big Cat in Reception and KS1 and Bug Club in KS2.
Phonics and Spelling:
In the Nursery we concentrate on developing children's speaking and listening skills and lay the foundations for the phonic work which starts in Reception. The children begin to explore sounds in the environment around them and develop their listening skills.
In Reception and Year 1, the children are taught phonics in whole class sessions. The whole school follows Mora Phonics, a systematic phonics programme based on 'Letters and Sounds' and the National Curriculum. The children are taught individual sounds, how to blend these sounds together to form words, how to segment the sounds for writing and how to form each grapheme to begin handwriting.
From Year 2 onwards, the children are taught spelling patterns and rules. Through three weekly spelling lessons, children learn how words are built — not just memorised! The spellings are often be linked to words that will be useful for the writing topic the children are working on, or common gaps that the teacher has identified. If a child is struggling to learn the spelling rules being taught, the class teacher may give them additional practice to complete at home.
Click here to go to our Mora Phonics resource page
Writing:
We use a range of exciting and stimulating books to engage children with literature and ensure they become familiar with writing styles from a wide selection of authors. The children are asked to write in a variety of genres; whether this is their own version of Shakespeare's Macbeth or writing their own instructions for how to catch The Enormous Crocodile! We view vocabulary, grammar and punctuation as the mechanics of writing and these are interwoven throughout daily English lessons. Our lessons are planned to support the children develop a process for writing through discussion of modelled texts, drama, working together and planning, as well as giving them time to review and edit their writing before publishing.

Breakfast and After-School Club
Breakfast Club 8:00-8:55am
Children are invited to join us for a nutritious breakfast and some exciting morning activities to set them up for their school day.
After-school Club 3:30-5:30pm
As well as a healthy snack, children coming to our after-school club will enjoy fun and engaging activities to round off their school day!
Costs
We offer a weekly discount for children attending all morning and afternoon sessions. We are a cashless school. All payments are taken on our online portal, Parent Mail.
Please speak with the school office for the most up-to-date costs.
To sign your child up, please contact the school office.

Extra-Curricular Activities
We aim to provide a wide range of extra-curricular activities for the children at Mora to broaden their experiences and enhance the curriculum.
Clubs are applied for on a termly basis and places are allocated fairly to ensure that as many children as possible have access to a club during the academic year. Contact the school office for a full list of clubs, costs and availability.

Art
Art at Mora
The Mora art curriculum helps children develop a range of ways in which they can explore their own creativity, whilst experimenting with different materials and learning about many art forms. Art lessons are about building confidence and instilling a ‘can do’ attitude, where all children are encouraged to have a go. We use art and creative expression as a tool to motivate, inspire and help bring academic learning to life.
Our curriculum stimulates the imagination by involving our children in a range of visual, tactile and sensory experiences, which enables them to communicate what they see, think and feel. It instills an appreciation and enjoyment of the visual arts and enables our children to develop a natural sense of wonder and curiosity about the world around them.
At Mora, we see every child as an artist and ensure that every one of our children has the opportunity to discover and nurture their own creativity. You only have to look at our children’s sketchbooks and take a walk through our colourful hallways to see the impact art has on everyone.
Every class (Years 1-6) has a weekly art lesson, taught by a specialist art teacher.

Geography
Geography at Mora
Geography at Mora aims to offer a curriculum that ensures a greater understanding of geographical and environmental factors in the world around us.
Teaching is stimulating, exciting and inclusive for all, providing children with key life skills such as teamwork, empathy, communication, language, thinking and independence skills which develop children both academically and socially.
Children are encouraged during lessons to become geographers, employing the skills that these professionals would need to study their chosen topic. A range of hands-on resources and activities are used to enhance the teaching of geography including trips, ICT, artefacts exploration and using subject specific equipment. These activities give children a greater understanding of their topics and they love getting their hands dirty!

History
History at Mora
The history curriculum aims to inform children of previous historical events, encouraging children to become historians during lessons, employing the skills that these professionals would need to study their chosen topic. A range of resources and activities are used to enhance the teaching of history including trips, ICT, artefacts exploration and using subject specific equipment. These activities give children a greater understanding of their topics and they love getting their hands dirty!
Teaching is stimulating, exciting and inclusive for all, providing children with key life skills such as teamwork, empathy, communication, language, thinking and independence skills which develop children both academically and socially.

Pupil Leaders
School Council
Mora's School Council comprises twelve class representatives, elected annually by the children in their classes. They meet regularly to represent the views of the pupils and to let adults know their feelings and opinions about things that affect them. They take an active part in helping to improve the school and have, for example, created a Friendship Bench for the playground following a pupil's suggestion. In addition, they organise events to benefit the local community, for example, encouraging donations for the local Food Bank. In the wider community, the children continue to organise support for charities such as Comic Relief. Each year the School Council visits the Houses of Parliament to learn about democracy.
House Captains
The House Captains play a vital role in fostering a sense of community and leadership among our students. House Captains are responsible for encouraging their peers to earn house points, which contribute to a friendly competition that promotes teamwork and school spirit. They present special awards in assemblies, collate house points, award lining up points and lead their houses on sports day.
Eco Warriors
At Mora Primary, we believe in instilling a sense of responsibility towards our environment in our students. Our Eco Warriors initiative encourages children to actively participate in recycling efforts by collecting paper and other recyclable materials used throughout the school day. Our Eco Warriors understand the importance of their actions in protecting our planet for future generations.
Play & Dance Leaders
Play and dance leaders are a group of Year 5 & 6 children who have been trained to organise activities for other children in the playground. They encourage children to join in games, create dance routines and extend their friendships. The leadership skills that they have been taught will also help to raise self-esteem, self -confidence and encourage physical activity.

Music
Music at Mora
At Mora, we want our children to have a broad and balanced curriculum where they learn new skills and have plenty of opportunities to be creative. Music is the perfect subject to engage and inspire children and allow them to discover their talents.
Music also helps to increase a child's self confidence and sense and achievement and enables them to express themselves in a different way.
Every class has a weekly music lesson, taught by a specialist music teacher.

Our Governors
Mora: Chair of Governors Statement
On behalf of the Governing Body, welcome to Mora Primary and Nursery School. We are a school that is passionate about making a difference in the lives of our children and our community, ensuring opportunities for all. At Mora our children, staff, parents, carers and governors work together to create an inclusive environment that is respectful of similarities and differences in all aspects of our diverse school. We live by our values to Aim high, Be resilient and Care for all.
As a Governing Body we provide both support and challenge across all areas of the school to ensure every child benefits from our vision and aims. As Governors, our most important role is ensuring the safety, welfare and education of our pupils.
The governing body consists of a balanced mix of parents, staff and representatives from the Local Authority and outside the school community. The full governing body, and our committees, meet regularly throughout each term, with the school’s leadership team, to ensure the smooth-running of all aspects of the school. We support the senior leadership team, teachers and staff in monitoring the children's progress and achievement, how teaching standards are set and maintained, how staff are managed, and how the school is kept safe for children and staff alike. We also monitor the ways in which the school spends its budget, and how that might best be allocated to get the best out of the school’s activities.
Mora’s Governing Body is committed to ensuring that each child at the school is given every chance to learn and develop in a safe, happy and nurturing environment. Mora has been judged a Good school by Ofsted for the last 10 years. We are incredibly proud that in our most recent Ofsted review (July 2024) we were rated Outstanding for Behaviour and attitudes and Personal development. Our result reflects the school’s incredible atmosphere, dedicated staff and their commitment to help each and every child achieve their full potential academically, emotionally and spiritually.
The Governing Body at Mora consists of:
Four parent Governors
Five co-opted Governors

Science
Science at Mora
At Mora Primary and Nursery School, we recognise the importance of science in every aspect of daily life. We deliver a hands on, enquiry based science curriculum; one that ignites curiosity and creates a sense of awe and wonder, while developing our children’s scientific concept of their world.
The teaching of science is driven by our science principles:
Foster Curiosity: Every science lesson is an opportunity to develop a sense of awe, wonder and curiosity.
By the end of KS2, our children will have a strong understanding of the world around them, and will have acquired specific skills and knowledge to help them to:
Think scientifically
Gain an understanding of scientific processes

Computing
Computing at Mora
At Mora, we believe that children will need to be "lifelong learners" with the confidence and ability to develop skills and understanding when meeting new challenges. Through the use of Purple Mash, the teaching of computing at Mora ensures that our children become confident and responsible users of information and communication technology.
Our vision is that a broad range of technologies will enrich the experience of all members of our community and that these resources will help to provide an environment without boundaries, where opportunities can be explored in safety and with confidence.
Computing is an integral part of the whole curriculum and children at Mora have access to class laptops, netbooks, iPads and a 30 computer lab room.

Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS)
The Early Years at Mora
The Early Years Foundation Stage at Mora is a welcoming and exciting place for children to learn and grow.
We offer a holistic approach to learning, focused around the key areas of young child's development. Children are given a wide variety of experiences, some that are led by adults and others that the children develop independently. Teaching through play is an integral part of the Early Years. Children are provided with a variety of opportunities to explore, experience and investigate. We encourage our children to take 'charge' of their learning and become independent learners.
The Early Years Foundation Stage is made up of Nursery and Reception. We have two part-time morning Nursery classes and two full time Reception classes. The children in the Nursery and Reception have the opportunity to learn and play together for part of their day.
